sentences.text: Emuarius was an extinct genus of flightless birds from Australia, commonly known as emuwaries.
The scientific name merges the words 'emu' and 'cassowary' to describe this creature.
Its anatomy was a mix, featuring a skull and femur like a cassowary alongside a lower leg and foot resembling an emu.
The species Emuarius gidju weighed an estimated 19 to 21 kilograms, which is less than a modern emu.
A second species named E. guljaruba is stated to be larger than Emuarius gidju.
The genus Emuarius was described in 1992 by Walter E. Boles.
A second species named E. guljaruba was described in 2001.
Emuarius is classified in the superorder Palaeognathae, order Casuariiformes, and family Casuariidae.
Phylogenetic analysis shows that Emuarius is a sister taxon to Dromaius.
Emuarius lived in Australia during the late Oligocene and middle Miocene, between 27.3 and 15.98 million years ago.
The validity of the second species E. guljaruba has been questioned until more fossil material is discovered.
